fieldNotes.location: Confirmed: 323 S County Road 300 W, Frankfort IN 46041. Roster point landed directly on the plant. Web research confirms two co-located Frito-Lay plants (Core Plant and East Plant) sharing the address — combined ~1100 employees, 17 snack production lines. Satellite shows a very large multi-building manufacturing campus with rooftop process equipment, on-site wastewater treatment ponds, bulk silos, a rail spur/yard, and extensive trailer yards. Frito-Lay monument sign visible at the SW entrance in 2026 Street View.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Campus is fenced (decorative metal fence visible along the County Road 300 W frontage in Street View). The entrance road has a checkpoint structure / guard booth at the point where it enters the secured plant area; classified as a controlled truck gate.
fieldNotes.guardShack: A small booth-footprint structure with a canopy sits on the entrance road at the secured-area boundary, consistent with a staffed guard booth. Medium confidence (resolved from satellite, not directly photographed), flagged.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Multiple large dock banks across both the Core and East plant buildings with many trailers backed in; aggregate well past 50.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Several large trailer drop yards (NW yard, an east-side yard, and a south yard) holding 150+ trailers in marked rows; 50+ band. dropYard true.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock clusters distributed across multiple, physically separate building faces of the two plants — shipping and receiving run from separate banks.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail spur/yard with multiple tracks and rail hopper cars runs onto the NE part of the property alongside bulk silos — confirmed rail-served for raw-material delivery.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Definitively a campus: two named plants (Core + East), plus a separate warehouse cluster to the north and support buildings — multiple large building clusters on one property.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide entrance apron and ample paved yard width leave clear room for a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge of Frankfort, IN, surrounded on multiple sides by agricultural fields — Rural.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~155 acres estimate for the built campus footprint (plants + yards + parking); the surrounding owned land including fields is larger.
